**8. INSPECTION SCOPE AND PROCEDURES**

The inspection shall cover the following areas and systems at the subject property, 4417 Alder Street, Meridian, OH 43901:

a) **Exterior envelope**: roof covering, gutters and downspouts, exterior walls and siding, foundation walls, porches, steps, and railings. Photographs shall be taken of any visible deterioration, sagging, or unsafe conditions.

b) **Interior common areas and dwelling units**: ceilings, walls, floors, windows and window sills, doors, and stairways. The inspector shall note any evidence of water intrusion, mold, peeling paint, or vermin infestation.

c) **Plumbing system**: visible piping, faucets, drains, water heater, and any evidence of leaks or sewage back-up. Water pressure shall be checked at the kitchen sink and at least one bathroom fixture in each unit.

d) **Electrical system**: visible wiring, outlet and switch plates, service panel access, and any exposed or frayed conductors. The inspector shall note any use of extension cords as a permanent wiring method.

e) **Heating system**: the furnace or boiler, radiators or registers, and thermostat operation. The inspection shall confirm that the heating system is capable of maintaining a temperature of at least 68 degrees Fahrenheit at a point three (3) feet above the floor in all habitable rooms.

f) **Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors**: presence and apparent operational status of detectors in each dwelling unit and in common hallways. The inspector shall note the location of each detector.

g) **Security and means of egress**: locks on all exterior doors, operation of windows intended for emergency egress, and the condition of any fire escapes.

The inspector shall complete ISD Inspection Form IF-2026-0441 during the inspection. The form requires documentation of each item listed above, including a condition rating of Satisfactory, Minor Defect, or Major Defect. Photographs shall be taken of all items rated Minor Defect or Major Defect, and of any item that is the subject of a tenant complaint. The inspector shall also complete a Photograph Log, listing each photograph in chronological order with a brief description of the subject.

**9. SPECIAL CONDITIONS AND REFERRALS**

The requesting party, Community Legal Aid Society, has submitted tenant complaints regarding the following conditions at 4417 Alder Street:

- Inadequate heat in the first-floor unit during the week of January 5, 2026
- Water staining on the ceiling of the second-floor bathroom
- A broken lock on the rear entrance door

- Evidence of lead-based paint hazards, which shall be referred to the Meridian Health Department Lead Program
- Structural conditions that may create an immediate safety hazard, which shall be referred to the Building and Codes Department
- Evidence of gas leaks or unsafe gas appliance operation, which shall be referred to the utility company and the Fire Prevention Bureau

Referrals shall be noted on the Inspection Form and in the inspector's summary to the ISD Supervisor. The inspector shall not make direct contact with other departments regarding referrals without prior approval from the ISD Supervisor.

**10. INSPECTION OF OTHER PROPERTIES**

a) **Lead-based paint testing**: When a property was constructed before 1978 and a child under six years of age resides in the dwelling, the Health Department may request a lead risk assessment. Sampling shall be limited to the areas identified in the request.

CITY OF LINCOLN — INSPECTION SERVICES DIVISION

Inspector: R. Delgado (ID# 4417)
Inspector Initials: RD

SECTION A – PROPERTY AND OCCUPANCY

Occupied at time of inspection: Yes
Number of adults present: 1 (tenant, Ms. A. Whitfield)
Number of children under 6: 1 (age 4)
Unit type: 3-bedroom apartment, second floor of three-story building
Building constructed: 1928 (per tax assessor records)
Heating system: Forced air, gas-fired; furnace located in basement
Hot water heater: 40-gallon, gas-fired

SECTION B – PURPOSE OF INSPECTION

Re-inspection of Unit 3B following a complaint filed with the City Hotline on
2026-01-05 (Complaint No. C-2026-0112). The complaint alleged peeling and chipping
paint in the living room and bedroom 1, and a report of a child with elevated blood
lead level. The initial inspection was conducted on 2026-01-14 by Inspector S. Patel
(IF-2026-0114). The purpose of this inspection is to document current conditions,
collect confirmation samples, and determine whether a lead-based paint hazard
exists as defined by 24 CFR 35.1320.

This inspection is also intended to verify repair status of previously cited
violations from a routine inspection dated 2025-11-03 (IF-2025-0892). See Section E
for status of those items.

SECTION C – VISUAL INSPECTION OBSERVATIONS

All rooms were visually inspected. Deteriorated paint was noted on the following
surfaces. The condition of each surface is coded as follows: P = peeling, C =
chipping, S = scaling, CR = cracking, D = deteriorated (general).

Living Room
- North window sash: paint is peeling and chipping along the lower edge of the
  sash. Condition: P, C. Approximate area: 3 in. x 12 in.
- North window frame: paint is cracked and peeling at the joint between the frame
  and the sash. Condition: P, CR. Approximate area: 2 in. x 8 in.
- Door frame leading to kitchen: paint is chipping at the base of the frame on the
  latch side. Condition: C. Approximate area: 1 in. x 4 in.
- Baseboard along north wall: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.
- West wall: no deteriorated paint observed.

Kitchen
- Countertop edge near the sink: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.
- Window sill: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.
- Door frame to hallway: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.
- Floor near the door frame: no paint chips observed on the floor.

Bedroom 1
- East window sash: paint is peeling and chipping along the upper edge of the
  sash. Condition: P, C. Approximate area: 2 in. x 10 in.
- Baseboard along east wall: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.
- Door frame: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.

Bedroom 2
- Door frame: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.
- Baseboard along south wall: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.
- Window sash: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.

Bathroom
- Door frame: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.
- Wall surface above the tub: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.

Hallway
- Baseboard along the west wall: paint is intact, no visible deterioration.

Other Observations:
- No evidence of moisture intrusion or water staining was observed in any room.
- No evidence of pests (rodents, cockroaches, or other insects) was observed.
- Ventilation in the bathroom was verified by operating the exhaust fan; the fan
  operates normally and vents to the exterior.
- The kitchen has a range hood that vents to the exterior; the hood was not
  operating at the time of inspection but was observed to be present and intact.

SECTION D – LEAD-BASED PAINT TESTING

D-1. XRF TESTING

XRF readings were collected on deteriorated and intact painted surfaces.
Instrument: Thermo Scientific Niton XL3t, Serial No. XL3-8891.
Calibration check performed prior to use: Pass.

XRF readings were collected on deteriorated and intact painted surfaces.
Instrument: Thermo Scientific Niton XL3t, Serial No. XL3-8891.
Calibration check performed prior to use: Pass.

Test results are reported in milligrams of lead per square centimeter (mg/cm²).
The regulatory action level for deteriorated paint is 1.0 mg/cm². Readings at or
above this level are considered positive for lead-based paint.

|---------|----------|-----------|-----------|------------------|--------|
| XRF-01 | Living room, west window sill | Wood | Intact | 0.02 | Negative |
| XRF-02 | Living room, west window sash | Wood | P | 0.04 | Negative |
| XRF-03 | Living room, east window sash | Wood | P, CR | 1.8 | Positive |

| XRF-10 | Hallway, baseboard west wall | Wood | Intact | 0.02 | Negative |

Notes on XRF Testing:
- XRF-03 and XRF-05 exceeded the action level. Both surfaces are deteriorated
  (peeling or chipping) and require stabilization and repainting or other
  abatement per ORC 3742.04.
- XRF-04 (0.9 mg/cm²) is below the action level but is close to the threshold.
  The paint is chipping. Recommend repainting the door frame as part of the
  repair work order, with a clearance dust wipe test after work is completed.
- All intact painted surfaces tested negative. No further testing is required
  for intact surfaces at this property.

D-2. DUST WIPE SAMPLING

Dust wipe samples were collected from floors and window sills in the living
room and bedroom 1, in accordance with HUD Guidelines, Chapter 7. Samples were
collected after the deteriorated paint surfaces were identified. Wipe media:
Lead Wipe™, Lot No. LW-26011.

Notes on Dust Wipe Sampling:
- DW-04 exceeded the clearance level for window sills. This is consistent with
  the deteriorated paint on the bedroom 1 window sash. The sill must be cleaned
  and retested after stabilization of the sash.
- All other dust wipe samples were below clearance levels.

No bare soil was present at the property. The property has a concrete walkway
and a small fenced patio with a concrete surface. No soil sampling was
performed.

No water testing was performed. The property is served by the municipal water
supply. No complaints of water quality were noted in the referral.
